awards.name: Most Valuable Player
awards.method: Blends Box Plus/Minus, win shares per 48 minutes, scoring and team winning percentage, the things MVP voters have historically rewarded. Players must have played at least 60% of their team's games and 28 minutes a night.

top.name: Victor Wembanyama
top.why: Victor Wembanyama is averaging 28.4 points, 12.0 rebounds and 3.3 assists for the San Antonio Spurs, who are 12–3 (3rd-best record in the league). He leads the league in Box Plus/Minus and win shares and ranks 3rd in scoring. That mix of individual production and team success makes him the front-runner.

top.name: Luka Dončić
top.why: Luka Dončić is averaging 38.1 points, 7.0 rebounds and 7.6 assists for the Los Angeles Lakers, who are 13–3 (the league's best record). He leads the league in scoring and ranks 3rd in Box Plus/Minus.

top.name: Alperen Şengün
top.why: Alperen Şengün is averaging 21.6 points, 9.1 rebounds and 6.8 assists for the Houston Rockets, who are 12–4 (4th-best record in the league). He ranks 5th in win shares.

top.name: Giannis Antetokounmpo
top.why: Giannis Antetokounmpo is averaging 28.2 points, 12.6 rebounds and 5.5 assists for the Miami Heat, who are 9–6 (13th-best record in the league). He ranks 4th in Box Plus/Minus and ranks 3rd in win shares.

top.why: Tyrese Maxey is averaging 26.5 points, 3.3 rebounds and 5.8 assists for the Philadelphia 76ers, who are 13–3 (2nd-best record in the league). He ranks 4th in win shares.

awards.name: Defensive Player of the Year
awards.method: Combines Defensive Box Plus/Minus, defensive win shares per 48 minutes, blocks, steals and how good the player's team defense is. Players must have played at least 60% of their team's games and 24 minutes a night.

top.why: Victor Wembanyama averages 4.1 blocks and 1.1 steals with a +5.0 Defensive BPM. He leads the league in Defensive Box Plus/Minus and defensive win shares. The San Antonio Spurs allow 107.6 points per 100 possessions, 2nd in the league.

awards.name: Rookie of the Year
awards.method: Weighs scoring, rebounds, assists, stocks (steals + blocks), Box Plus/Minus and role size among first-year players who have appeared in at least half their team's games.

top.name: Darius Acuff Jr.
top.why: Darius Acuff Jr. is averaging 26.2 points, 3.6 rebounds and 7.0 assists in 36.7 minutes. He leads all rookies in scoring. He's the rookie to beat right now.

top.name: Yaxel Lendeborg
top.why: Yaxel Lendeborg is averaging 20.3 points, 7.3 rebounds and 3.5 assists in 31.6 minutes. He's 2nd among rookies in scoring. He's also been a positive on the floor (+0.7 BPM), which is rare for a first-year player.

top.name: Cameron Boozer
top.why: Cameron Boozer is averaging 16.6 points, 9.4 rebounds and 5.3 assists in 31.1 minutes. He's also been a positive on the floor (+1.4 BPM), which is rare for a first-year player.

awards.name: Most Improved Player
awards.method: Compares each player's points, rebounds, assists, steals and blocks per game with last season (at least 20 games then), with credit for a bigger role and a small penalty for players who were already stars.

top.name: Terrence Shannon Jr.
top.why: Terrence Shannon Jr. has gone from 5.6 points, 1.1 rebounds and 0.9 assists last season to 12.9 / 3.3 / 2.9. A bigger role (12 → 23 minutes) explains part of the jump.

top.name: Davion Mitchell
top.why: Davion Mitchell has gone from 9.3 points, 2.7 rebounds and 6.5 assists last season to 17.2 / 2.4 / 9.0. A bigger role (29 → 36 minutes) explains part of the jump.

top.name: Dylan Harper
top.why: Dylan Harper has gone from 11.8 points, 3.4 rebounds and 3.9 assists last season to 18.4 / 5.4 / 4.5. A bigger role (23 → 32 minutes) explains part of the jump.

top.why: Franz Wagner has gone from 20.6 points, 5.2 rebounds and 3.3 assists last season to 24.4 / 6.9 / 8.5. A bigger role (30 → 37 minutes) explains part of the jump. Voters tend to favor breakouts over players who were already stars.
